summaries:
The chapter opens with Della counting her meager savings of one dollar and eighty-seven cents—mostly pennies—on the eve of Christmas, realizing she cannot afford a meaningful gift for her husband, Jim. She lives in a modest, run-down flat rented for $8 per week, where the letterbox and electric button are nonfunctional, and the once-proud name 'James Dillingham Young' has been reduced to 'Jim' in daily life. After a moment of despair, Della makes the drastic decision to sell her most prized possession—her long, beautiful brown hair—to buy Jim a platinum fob chain for his cherished gold pocket watch, which he keeps on an old leather strap. She returns home with eighty-seven cents and spends hours curling her shortened hair into a boyish style, anxious about Jim’s reaction. When Jim arrives home, he is stunned silent at the sight of her cut hair, not from anger but disbelief; moments later, he reveals he has sold his watch to buy her a set of exquisite tortoiseshell combs she had long admired in a Broadway window. They realize their gifts are now useless, yet they embrace, recognizing the profound love behind their sacrifices.
[Characters: Della, Jim, Madame Sofronie, James Dillingham Young, Queen of Sheba, King Solomon]
